Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of Summit HealthTech's procurement for patient-facing summarization, we need a short performance questionnaire to validate latency and scaling behavior for the PoC. Please see the attached spreadsheet (scaleproof-test-plan.csv) and provide the following by EOD Wednesday if possible:

- P50/P95 token latency (ms) for 256/512/1024 prompt lengths for the model variant you recommend for summarization.
- Maximum concurrent open sessions and observed throughput (tokens/sec) during sustained 30-minute runs.
- Startup (cold) vs. warm (KV-cache primed) latency deltas and Kv-cache hit-rate assumptions.
- Autoscaling behavior: expected time-to-scale and guidance for concurrency headroom to maintain p95 SLO.
- Any model quantization or batching trade-offs we should be aware of for patient data (no PII in model store).

We will include your responses in the RFP Appendix B. Also please attach any short test scripts or configurations you used.

Best,
Eleanor Park
Procurement Lead, Summit HealthTech

Eleanor — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching our two-pager and a small test matrix (test-matrix.yaml) plus the CSV you sent with our suggested acceptance criteria. High level answers below; detailed numbers and scripts attached.

Quick answers (summary):
- Recommended model variant: rwd-7B-tuned-summarize (8-bit quantized option available for cost-sensitive bursts).
- Latency (example p50/p95 for 512 tokens, NVidia A100 40GB, batch size 1, single-stream): ~42ms / ~105ms per token (generation token); end-to-end response for 512 prompt + 128 generation typically 450–900ms depending on output length and cache state. Detailed table in redwood_latency_report_q2.pdf.
- Throughput (sustained 30-min runs): with a 4-GPU dedicated shard we observed ~45k tokens/sec aggregate (batching to 8), scaling linearly with added shards in our tests; per-GPU sustain ~11–12k tokens/sec. See test-matrix.yaml for concurrency curves.
- Cold vs Warm: cold-start additional latency ~700–1200ms for process/container spin-up; warm (KV primed) p95 improves by ~15–35% depending on request locality. We include measurement methodology.
- Autoscaling guidance: recommend target headroom of 25–30% over observed peak concurrency to keep p95 under 1s; typical scale-out latency is 60–90s for dedicated pool (faster for burst capacity).
- Quantization/tradeoffs: int8/4 quantization reduces memory and cost but can raise p95 by ~10–20ms per token and requires our QA eval set; we list recommended eval thresholds.

I’ve looped in Jonas for the detailed methodology and the exact test harness (scripts).

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Eleanor — hi, Jonas from the benchmarks team here. Quick technical clarifications inline below; forwarding as Vanessa asked.

1) KV pre-warm: for PoC we ship a small cache-priming script that runs a set of representative prefix queries across the model to populate the KV cache. In our dedicated pools the cache is shared per model-shard process and persists until the process exits; across container restarts the cache is cold. For longer-lived Dedicated setups we recommend a keep-alive ping policy (every 10–15 minutes) if you need to keep processes warm.

2) Scaling policy used in the 4-GPU run: horizontal scaling (adding identical shards) was used. Each shard allowed up to 12 concurrent generation streams; autoscaler triggers at 75% per-shard CPU/GPU util or sustained queueing latency >120ms for 30s window. For vertical (per-shard concurrency) increases we use conservative caps to avoid memory pressure; horizontal scaling is preferred for predictable p95 behavior. Config snippets attached in test-matrix.yaml.

3) Isolation: the reported 4-GPU sustained numbers were from a Redwood Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated nodes) — not multi-tenant hosted. For hosted multi-tenant we publish peak-per-tenant SLOs (see PDF appendix) but isolation guarantees differ and we note them in the RFP reply.

Logs: we can provide raw logs in CSV with per-token timestamps, GPU utilization series (1s granularity), and histogram buckets for latencies. We also provide a JSON-formatted trace per request (request_id, token_offsets, timing_breakdown). Sample export: attached sample_logs_summary.csv and sample_trace.json (small).

If you want, we can run a 2-hour PoC run with Polaris present and stream metrics live. We typically provision a small Dedicated pool for that exercise.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
